diagnosticContract: symptom -> plausible mechanisms -> discriminating evidence -> controlled test -> interpretation -> possible corrective action

sourceSeeds.title: Injection Molding Troubleshooter
sourceSeeds.scope: Initial, non-binding troubleshooting guidance covering short shot, flash, sink marks, voids, moisture streaks, burning, weld lines, warpage and black specks.

sourceSeeds.title: Ultramid PA product brochure — processing by injection moulding
sourceSeeds.scope: Polyamide-family processing guidance including moisture and thermal-history considerations; grade-specific data remains controlling.

sourceSeeds.title: Ultrason Injection Molding
sourceSeeds.scope: Ultrason-family processing/troubleshooting guidance including moisture/silver streak and residence-time effects.

sourceSeeds.issuer: The International Journal of Advanced Manufacturing Technology
sourceSeeds.title: A review of research progress on the minimization of weld lines in injection molding
sourceSeeds.scope: Review of weld-line formation, influencing factors, mechanisms, prediction and improvement methods; does not establish a universal fix.

sourceSeeds.title: Standard Test Method of Measuring Shrinkage from Mold Dimensions of Thermoplastics
sourceSeeds.scope: Thermoplastic moulding shrinkage test method and limitations of extrapolating standard specimens to production parts.

sourceSeeds.title: Plastics and rubber machines — Injection moulding machines — Safety requirements
sourceSeeds.scope: Injection-moulding-machine safety requirements and safe-use information.

claims.claim: A defect should be defined by observable location, frequency, cavity/time pattern and severity before settings are changed.
claims.exclusions: Site-specific defect classification may add criteria.
claims.basis: Manufacturer troubleshooting is organized by observable defect classes, but the full measurement protocol is a MouldMaster diagnostic discipline rather than a controlling supplier rule.

claims.claim: Similar visible defects can arise from different material, machine, mould and process mechanisms, so one symptom should not be treated as a unique root cause.
claims.exclusions: Some measured failures can become uniquely diagnostic with sufficient evidence.
claims.basis: BASF presents multiple possible causes/actions for the same defect classes, directly supporting competing-mechanism reasoning.

claims.claim: Corrective changes should be selected as controlled, safe tests that discriminate among hypotheses rather than simultaneous guesswork.
claims.exclusions: Emergency/safety actions follow site procedure, not experiments.
claims.basis: Supplier guidance supports cause/action testing, but formal controlled-experiment methodology is better grounded in the separate NIST evidence used in the engineering audit.

claims.claim: A short shot establishes incomplete cavity filling but does not by itself identify why filling stopped.
claims.exclusions: Intentional short-shot studies are excluded.
claims.basis: BASF recognizes short shot as a defect class with multiple possible causes rather than one cause.

claims.claim: Short shot can be associated with delivery, transfer, flow resistance, venting, thermal/material condition or machine-delivery limitations.
claims.exclusions: The listed mechanisms are possibilities, not exhaustive or guaranteed.
claims.basis: Manufacturer troubleshooting supports multiple flow/process/material causes; machine-specific failure mechanisms still require equipment documentation.

claims.claim: Pressure/temperature should not be increased indiscriminately before checking repeatability, shot delivery, fill pattern, material preparation and restrictions.
claims.exclusions: A verified cause may justify a targeted parameter change.
claims.basis: Supplier guidance recommends multiple cause-specific checks/actions; MouldMaster's ordered evidence workflow is intentionally more conservative than the source.

claims.claim: Flash is polymer outside the intended cavity boundary and can occur when melt enters or opens an unintended gap under the actual pressure/thermal/rheological condition.
claims.exclusions: Intentional film gates/overflow features are not defects.
claims.basis: Manufacturer troubleshooting identifies flash and links it to process/tooling/clamping conditions.

claims.claim: Tool condition, clamping condition, cavity pressure/packing, melt viscosity and contamination at shutoffs can create similar flash symptoms.
claims.exclusions: Any individual mould may have a narrower cause set.
claims.basis: Multiple process and mould causes are supported; machine-specific clamp behavior and tooling damage assessment remain external.

claims.claim: Flash location and onset timing should be used to separate a tooling condition from process-pressure history before simply increasing clamp force.
claims.exclusions: Does not define a clamp-setting procedure.
claims.basis: Source supports both tooling and processing causes; the explicit location/time discrimination method is a conservative inference requiring technical review.

claims.claim: Local volumetric contraction during cooling contributes to sink/void formation, particularly in thick or thermally isolated regions.
claims.exclusions: Mechanism details vary with material, geometry and pressure history.
claims.basis: Shrinkage standard and troubleshooting guidance support contraction-related behaviour; local mechanics are geometry/process specific.

claims.section: Surface sink and internal void are different outcomes
claims.claim: Local contraction may appear as surface depression or internal void depending on shell stiffness, geometry and pressure transmission.
claims.exclusions: Not a universal binary mechanism for every material/geometry.
claims.basis: BASF treats sink marks and voids as distinct but related defect classes; the shell-mechanics explanation needs a dedicated polymer-processing reference before full support.

claims.claim: Gate effectiveness, packing response, wall-thickness transitions and cooling should be evaluated before generic pressure/time increases.
claims.exclusions: Specific validated processes may have known corrective responses.
claims.basis: ASTM identifies packing and thermal conditions as shrinkage influences; BASF includes geometry/process factors for sink and void troubleshooting.

claims.section: Appearance is not a unique diagnosis
claims.claim: Silver streaks/splay can be associated with moisture or other volatiles but similar appearance can arise from air, contamination or thermal degradation.
claims.exclusions: Material-specific appearance modes vary.
claims.basis: BASF separates moisture streaks, burning streaks, colored streaks and related defects and provides multiple mechanisms.

claims.claim: Moisture-related diagnosis should confirm exact material identity, handling history and current grade-specific moisture/drying requirements.
claims.exclusions: Not all splay is moisture-related.
claims.basis: Manufacturer guidance makes drying/moisture limits material- and grade-dependent.

claims.claim: Hotter/longer drying is not universally safer because excessive thermal exposure can damage some materials; supplier conditions control.
claims.exclusions: Exact over-drying risk depends on grade/dryer.
claims.basis: Manufacturer sources establish grade-specific thermal/drying windows; the exact over-drying failure mechanism varies by material.

claims.claim: Dark/burned areas can result from trapped/compressed gas or degraded material, so appearance alone is not a unique diagnosis.
claims.exclusions: Other contamination mechanisms may also exist.
claims.basis: BASF separately documents diesel effect/burning, burning streaks and black-speck/degradation mechanisms.

claims.claim: A repeatable end-of-fill mark supports a different hypothesis set from intermittent degraded/black material after stoppage.
claims.exclusions: Pattern is evidence, not proof of one cause.
claims.basis: Defect-location/process-state distinctions are consistent with manufacturer troubleshooting but require measured confirmation in the actual mould.

claims.claim: Venting/fill behaviour should be investigated for trapped-gas hypotheses, while residence/temperature/material/dead-zone evidence should be investigated for degradation hypotheses.
claims.exclusions: No generic machine intervention or vent dimension is authorized.
claims.basis: Manufacturer sources distinguish gas/venting and thermal/degradation cause families.

claims.claim: Weld/knit regions form where separate melt fronts meet after being divided by geometry or multiple flow paths/gates.
claims.exclusions: Terminology can distinguish weld vs meld/knit configurations.
claims.basis: Recent peer-reviewed review specifically addresses weld-line formation mechanisms.

claims.section: Quality depends on the meeting conditions
claims.claim: Weld-region appearance/strength can depend on thermal, pressure, flow-front, orientation, gas and material conditions rather than one variable.
claims.exclusions: Dominant factors depend on material and geometry.
claims.basis: Review covers multiple influencing factors/mechanisms and weld-line quality outcomes.

claims.section: Treat location as a design-process interaction
claims.claim: Changing a weld region can require coordinated gate, geometry, venting, material and process changes; a single temperature increase is not a universal fix.
claims.exclusions: A specific validated case may have one dominant corrective action.
claims.basis: Independent review and manufacturer troubleshooting both present multi-factor mitigation rather than one universal fix.

claims.claim: Black specks can indicate foreign or degraded material, including contamination, stagnant/degraded polymer or incompatible residue.
claims.exclusions: Appearance alone cannot identify the source.
claims.basis: Manufacturer troubleshooting explicitly covers black specks and degradation/contamination cause families.

claims.claim: Occurrence pattern relative to downtime, cavity, lot or material handling can help discriminate likely sources.
claims.exclusions: Pattern does not prove root cause without confirming evidence.
claims.basis: The source supports multiple source mechanisms, but the explicit temporal/cavity discrimination framework is MouldMaster synthesis.

claims.section: Do not create a safety problem while diagnosing
claims.claim: Hot purging, nozzle/barrel work and disassembly require approved machine/material procedures rather than improvised cleaning.
claims.applicability: Interventions involving hot pressurised polymer or machine access.
claims.exclusions: This Book does not define the procedure.
claims.basis: Safety direction is appropriate, but verification requires applicable machine-manufacturer purge/service instructions and site isolation procedures.

summary.rule: No troubleshooting chapter may imply symptom-to-cause certainty or a guaranteed fix; hold blocks promotion.
